title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark for Runtime Security Risks in Workspace Agents
title_zh: EvoRiskBench: 一个针对工作空间代理运行时安全风险的 evolving benchmark

paragraphs.en: Workspace agents combine large language models with execution harnesses to perform stateful, multi-step tasks that access or modify external resources. Existing benchmarks leave gaps in executable coverage of their runtime security risks, while evolving model capabilities, harnesses, tools, and threats motivate benchmark evolution. We introduce EvoRiskBench , an evolving benchmark organized around the EP–Path–EF framework, which links an initial risk entry point to an one-hop technical effect through an agent-mediated risk path. The framework defines nine entry-point categories and five effect categories; a 20-participant study supports their interpretability and classification consistency on representative cases. Guided by this framework, an automated end-to-end workflow constructs and executes risk cases in isolated environments and independently verifies outcomes using runtime traces and environment states. The benchmark provides a reproducible dataset of 450 adversarial tasks across six scenarios. We evaluate nine Model × \times Harness configurations spanning three models (GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, and Claude Opus 5) and three harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw). Our results reveal substantial vulnerabilities across systems. The most vulnerable configuration, Codex with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, reaches a 68.44% attack success rate (ASR), indicating that configuration of workspace agent is insufficient to ensure secure autonomous execution. ASR varies more across models than harnesses, and harness differences depend on the model. The benchmark cases and evaluation platform will be released after completion of artifact safety and reproducibility checks.
paragraphs.zh: 工作区智能体将大型语言模型与执行框架相结合，以执行需要访问或修改外部资源的有状态多步骤任务。 现有的基准测试在执行覆盖范围方面对其运行时安全风险存在空白，而不断发展的模型能力、执行框架、工具和威胁则推动了基准测试的演进。 我们提出了 EvoRiskBench——一个基于 EP–Path–EF 框架的演进式基准测试，该框架通过智能体中介的风险路径，将初始风险入口点与单跳技术影响关联起来。 该框架定义了九类入口点和五类影响；一项包含 20 名参与者的研究验证了其在典型案例上的可解释性和分类一致性。 在该框架的指导下，一个自动化端到端工作流程可在隔离环境中构建并执行风险案例，同时利用运行时追踪和环境状态独立验证结果。 该基准测试提供了一个可复现的数据集，包含六个场景中的 450 个对抗性任务。 我们评估了九种模型 × 执行框架的组合配置，涵盖三种模型（GPT-5.6 Sol、DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 和 Claude Opus 5）以及三种执行框架（Claude Code、Codex 和 OpenClaw）。 我们的研究结果揭示了各系统之间存在严重的安全漏洞。 最脆弱的配置是 Codex 与 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 的组合，其攻击成功率（ASR）高达 68.44%，表明仅靠工作区智能体的配置不足以确保安全的自主执行。 攻击成功率在不同模型间的差异大于不同执行框架间的差异，且执行框架的差异取决于所用模型。 基准测试案例和评估平台将在完成成果安全性和可复现性检查后发布。

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that execute multi-step tasks through interaction with tools and external environments ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . We refer to workspace agent as stateful Model × \times Harness systems that pursue user-delegated tasks through successive observations and tool-mediated actions, accessing or modifying external resources and state . This formulation subsumes API-based tool agents and GUI-based computer-use agents ( Rawles et al., 2025 ) as interface-specific instances of LLM agents, while emphasizing persistent state, orchestration, permissions, and heterogeneous resources. The harness manages context, execution state, tool interfaces, permissions, and orchestration, mediating how model-selected actions are executed in the environment. Unlike response-only conversational systems, workspace agents can turn model outputs into operations with direct technical effects on external resources. We therefore focus on runtime security risks arising from agent execution, assessing both observable execution behavior and its direct, verifiable technical effects.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地被部署为自主智能体，这些智能体通过与工具及外部环境交互来执行多步骤任务（Wang 等人，2024）。 我们将工作空间智能体定义为具备状态保持能力的模型 × Harness 系统，这些系统通过连续观察和工具中介行动来执行用户委托的任务，并访问或修改外部资源与状态。 这一框架将基于 API 的工具智能体和基于 GUI 的计算机使用智能体（Rawles 等人，2025）视为 LLM 智能体的特定接口实例，同时强调持续状态、协调机制、权限以及异构资源。 Harness 负责管理上下文、执行状态、工具接口、权限和协调机制，并中介模型所选动作在环境中的执行方式。 与仅生成响应的对话系统不同，工作空间智能体能够将模型输出转化为操作，从而对外部资源产生直接的技术影响。 因此，我们重点关注智能体执行过程中产生的运行时安全风险，评估其可观察的执行行为及其直接且可验证的技术影响。

paragraphs.en: Agent-security evaluation has broadened to cover explicitly harmful multi-step tasks ( Andriushchenko et al., 2025 ) , indirect prompt injection (IPI) in tool-using environments ( Debenedetti et al., 2024 ) , and trajectory-dependent harms that emerge through accumulated context and tool-mediated execution ( Feng et al., 2026a ) . Recent work further structures risk entries and impacts, organizes lifecycle evidence, and automates risk discovery and verification ( Li et al., 2026b ; Zhou et al., 2026 ; Feng et al., 2026b ) . However, executable coverage of workspace-agent runtime risks remains incomplete: risks entering through agent communication and subagent delegation have only partial or no identified coverage in the compared benchmarks, while coverage of technical effects such as resource exhaustion is uneven (Table 1 ). Moreover, testing a technical effect through one entry interface does not establish coverage of other interfaces or execution paths that may lead to the same effect. A fixed set of test cases may also become less representative as model capabilities, harnesses, tools, and threats evolve. Beyond coverage, reliable evaluation requires monitoring the workspace during execution to corroborate technical effects that may not be fully captured by agent-visible trajectories or final-state checks.

paragraphs.en: Building on this representation, EvoRiskBench provides an automated end-to-end workflow for Risk Path generation and independent system-level evaluation. Execution traces and replay-verification feedback guide adversarial refinement and subsequent case generation. The same workflow supports extending the benchmark with additional validated cases as model capabilities, harnesses, tools, and threats evolve. paragraphs.en: A unified platform for workspace-agent runtime evaluation and verification. We build isolated and resettable Windows-based Docker environments for executing identical benchmark cases across nine Model × \times Harness configurations . The platform instantiates all nine risk entry points through native runtime interfaces, and covers five risk effects . Execution trajectories and independently collected environment evidence support verification of the targeted technical effects. The EP–EF decomposition further reveals concentrations of risk that aggregate scores obscure, providing a basis for comparing complete agent configurations and targeting defensive evaluation at specific runtime interfaces.

paragraphs.en: Tool-using LLM agents interact with external environments through APIs and other tools ( Schick et al., 2023 ; Yao et al., 2023 ; Yao et al., 2025 ) , while computer-use agents extend this interaction to graphical and operating-system interfaces ( Rawles et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) . These interface-specific agents can also be viewed as instances of a broader class of workspace agents: systems that pursue user-delegated tasks in evolving environments containing files, code, tools, external services, and persistent state ( Zhou et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ; Jimenez et al., 2024 ) . Their behavior is jointly determined by the model and its harness, which manages context, execution state, tool interfaces, permissions, and orchestration. The same model may therefore exhibit different runtime behavior across harnesses. Following this perspective, EvoRiskBench evaluates complete, stateful Model × \times Harness configurations, examining risks arising as agents access or modify external resources during task execution.

paragraphs.en: AgentHarm evaluates explicitly harmful task completion ( Andriushchenko et al., 2025 ) , while ToolEmu examines agent risks in sandboxed tool-use settings ( Ruan et al., 2024 ) . AgentDojo, InjecAgent, and WASP study indirect prompt injection ( Debenedetti et al., 2024 ; Zhan et al., 2024 ; Evtimov et al., 2025 ) . ASB further covers attacks such as memory poisoning and backdoors ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . AgentHazard and AgentS4D emphasize complete execution trajectories and runtime risks across the agent lifecycle ( Feng et al., 2026a ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) , while AgentCanary evaluates agent security in executable environments ( Li et al., 2026b ) . OpenAgentSafety further provides a broader framework for evaluating real-world agent safety ( Vijayvargiya et al., 2026 ) . Related analyses examine layered attack surfaces and inconsistencies across benchmark risk taxonomies ( Chu, 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ) . These efforts provide complementary threat models and ways of organizing risk. EvoRiskBench focuses on risks indirectly induced through untrusted workspace content, using an EP–Path–EF representation to connect entry points, agent-mediated execution paths, and direct technical effects. Since one entry point can lead to different effects and the same effect can arise through different paths, representing both dimensions supports executable case construction and coverage analysis. paragraphs.en: Fixed test suites may become less representative as agent capabilities, harnesses, and tools evolve, motivating evaluation methods that continually extend and refine cases ( Chen et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) . Dynamic risk assessment studies iterative improvement of offensive agents ( Wei et al., 2025 ) , while GPT-Red uses scalable self-play to discover prompt-injection attacks across models and harnesses ( Wallace et al., 2026 ) . Vera further automates risk discovery, executable case construction, and evidence-grounded verification, using execution feedback to guide subsequent exploration ( Feng et al., 2026b ) . Building on this direction, EvoRiskBench organizes adversarial case construction through EP–Path–EF constraints. Execution feedback collected under a fixed Model × \times Harness configuration guides case refinement, while validated cases and observed failure modes inform subsequent generation. This workflow supports continued expansion with additional validated cases. Case refinement occurs during construction, while formal evaluation uses a frozen case set across Model × \times Harness configurations.

paragraphs.en: Workspace-agent risks cannot be fully characterized by attack techniques alone. The same adversarial technique may enter an agent through different runtime interfaces and propagate through different execution paths, while the same entry interface may lead to different technical consequences depending on agent behavior, permissions, and environmental context ( Liu et al., 2024 ) . Therefore, we represent runtime risks through two primary dimensions: a risk entry point ( E ​ P EP ) and a risk effect ( E ​ F EF ). The relationship between these two dimensions is instantiated through an agent-mediated risk path during execution.
paragraphs.zh: 工作区智能体的风险无法仅通过攻击技术完全描述。 相同的对抗性技术可能通过不同的运行时接口进入智能体，并沿不同的执行路径传播；同时，根据智能体的行为、权限和环境上下文，相同的入口接口也可能导致不同的技术后果（Liu 等人，2024）。 因此，我们通过两个主要维度来表示运行时风险：风险入口点（E​P EP）和风险影响（E​F EF）。 这两个维度之间的关系在执行过程中通过智能体介导的风险路径得以具体实现。

paragraphs.en: We consider only IPI attacks in which an attacker can place or manipulate malicious content in an untrusted workspace resource exposed to the agent through a risk entry point, while the user provides a benign task. Beyond controlling this untrusted content, the attacker cannot modify trusted system or developer instructions, model parameters, harness implementations, environment configurations, or verification components; directly invoke tools or perform the target operation; or forge execution evidence. Direct compromise of the model or harness is outside our scope. Any harmful effect must therefore arise through Model × \times Harness execution.
paragraphs.zh: 我们仅考虑 IPI 攻击，即攻击者可以通过风险入口点，在暴露给智能体的不可信工作空间资源中放置或操控恶意内容，而用户则提供一个良性任务。 除了控制这些不可信内容外，攻击者无法修改受信任的系统或开发者指令、模型参数、执行器实现、环境配置或验证组件；无法直接调用工具或执行目标操作；也无法伪造执行证据。 对模型或执行器的直接破坏不在我们的研究范围内。 因此，任何有害影响都必须通过“模型 × 执行器”的执行过程产生。

paragraphs.en: We identify nine risk entry points by locating where adversarial influence enters or becomes actionable during workspace-agent execution, following the layered attack-surface perspective ( Chu, 2026 ) . As summarized in Table 2 , these entry points span four broad attack surfaces: memory and retrieval , tool and execution , multi-agent collaboration , and the agent ecosystem . This organization supports systematic coverage of runtime risk beyond specific attack techniques.

paragraphs.en: Prior agent-security benchmarks characterize harmful outcomes by their impact on data, system state, and resources ( Li et al., 2026b ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) . Building on these taxonomies and the CIA security properties, we define five effect categories, summarized in Table 3 . Each category captures a one-hop technical effect : an observable and verifiable consequence directly produced by agent execution, regardless of how many actions are required to realize it. For example, in a Data Tampering case ( e ​ f 3 ef_{3} ), overwriting a configuration file constitutes the directly verifiable effect; any subsequent service failure is a downstream consequence and does not alter the pre-specified effect label.
paragraphs.zh: 早期的智能体安全基准通过其对数据、系统状态和资源的影响来界定有害结果（Li et al., 2026b；Zhou et al., 2026）。 基于这些分类体系和CIA安全属性，我们定义了五种影响类别，如表3所示。 每个类别都捕捉一种单跳技术影响：即由智能体执行直接产生的、可观察且可验证的后果，无论实现该后果需要多少动作。 例如，在数据篡改案例（e f 3 ef_{3}）中，覆盖配置文件即为可直接验证的影响；任何后续的服务故障都是下游后果，并不会改变预先指定的影响标签。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate each valid attack run using three complementary metrics. Let N N denote the number of valid runs, and let k i , u i ∈ { 0 , 1 } k_{i},u_{i}\in\{0,1\} indicate whether the i i -th run achieves its attacker-defined goal and successfully completes the legitimate user task, respectively. The Attack Success Rate (ASR) is defined as ASR = 1 N ​ ∑ i = 1 N k i \mathrm{ASR}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}k_{i} . The Task Success Rate (TSR) is defined as TSR = 1 N ​ ∑ i = 1 N u i \mathrm{TSR}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}u_{i} , measuring the proportion of legitimate user tasks successfully completed in the presence of an indirect prompt injection. To assess the severity of harmful behavior observed in the execution trajectory of each benchmark run, we additionally report a Harm Score (HS) . An evidence-grounded judge assigns each trajectory a score h i ∈ [ 0 , 10 ] h_{i}\in[0,10] based on the agent’s actions, tool outputs, security alerts, and system-level evidence. We report the mean score across runs with valid trajectory-level judgments. A score of 0 0 indicates that no harmful behavior is observed, while higher scores indicate increasingly severe harmful behavior. High scores require corroborating execution or system-level evidence.

paragraphs.en: Among the 4,050 attack executions across all nine Model × \times Harness configurations, 1,517 successfully achieve their respective attacker-defined goals through workspace-agent execution, yielding an aggregate ASR of 37.46%. This vulnerability is not confined to any single configuration: five of the six configurations using GPT-5.6 Sol or DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 achieve ASRs of at least 50%, spanning all three harnesses. The combination of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 and Codex achieves the highest ASR, reaching 68.44%. These results show that malicious instructions embedded in untrusted workspace content can propagate through the agent execution chain and ultimately produce observable state changes in external resources. IPI poses a non-negligible runtime security risk to workspace agents.
paragraphs.zh: 在所有九种 Model × Harness 配置中，共执行了 4,050 次攻击操作，其中 1,517 次通过工作区-智能体执行成功实现了攻击者设定的各自目标，综合 ASR 达到 37.46%。 这种漏洞并不局限于任何单一配置：使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 或 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 的六种配置中有五种，其 ASR 均至少达到 50%，且覆盖了全部三种 harness。 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 与 Codex 的组合实现了最高的 ASR，达到了 68.44%。 这些结果表明，嵌入在不可信工作区内容中的恶意指令可以通过智能体执行链传播，并最终在外部资源中产生可观察的状态变化。 IPI 对工作区智能体构成了不可忽略的运行时安全风险。

paragraphs.en: The aggregated ASRs of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5 are 58.81%, 49.11%, and 4.44%, respectively. The resulting 54.37-percentage-point model-level spread is substantially larger than the 5.41-percentage-point spread among the harness-level averages, indicating that model choice is the primary source of ASR variation. Inspection of unsuccessful trajectories suggests that the consistently low ASRs of Claude Opus 5 are partly attributable to its cyber-safety mechanisms, which frequently refuse or interrupt operations that pose real-world system risks. Nevertheless, the harness remains consequential. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 exhibits higher ASRs than GPT-5.6 Sol with OpenClaw and Codex, whereas GPT-5.6 Sol achieves a slightly higher ASR with Claude Code (52.44% vs. 51.56%), indicating that harness effects are model dependent. These results highlight the importance of evaluating workspace-agent security at the level of the complete Model × \times Harness system.
paragraphs.zh: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813、GPT-5.6 Sol 和 Claude Opus 5 的聚合 ASR 分别为 58.81%、49.11% 和 4.44%。 由此产生的模型层面 54.37 个百分点的差距，远大于测试框架层面平均值之间 5.41 个百分点的差距，表明模型选择是 ASR 差异的主要来源。 对失败轨迹的分析显示，Claude Opus 5 持续偏低的 ASR 部分归因于其网络安全机制，该机制经常拒绝或中断可能引发现实世界系统风险的操作。 尽管如此，测试框架仍然具有重要影响。 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 在使用 OpenClaw 和 Codex 时的 ASR 高于 GPT-5.6 Sol，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 在使用 Claude Code 时则略高（52.44% vs. 51.56%），表明测试框架的影响因模型而异。 这些结果凸显了在完整的“模型 × 测试框架”系统层面评估工作空间-智能体安全性的重要性。

paragraphs.en: We present EvoRiskBench, an execution-grounded benchmark for runtime security risks in workspace agents under IPI. It characterizes risk through nine entry points and five verifiable effects, instantiated by 450 executable benchmark cases. Its execution-feedback-driven construction and verification workflow supports case refinement and versioned expansion, while cross-configuration evaluation uses a frozen, shared case set. Across 4,050 runs over nine Model × \times Harness configurations, EvoRiskBench reports 37.46% ASR and 60.44% TSR. ASR varies more across models than harnesses, and harness differences depend on the model. ASRs differ across entry points and effects, while task utility varies across configurations. These results support joint security-utility evaluation of complete workspace agents and motivate runtime defenses.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 EvoRiskBench，这是一个基于执行的基准测试，用于评估 IPI 环境下工作空间智能体在运行时面临的安全风险。 该基准通过九个入口点和五个可验证的影响来刻画风险，并由 450 个可执行的基准案例具体实现。 其以执行反馈为驱动的建设与验证流程支持案例的优化和版本化扩展，而跨配置评估则使用一个固定且共享的案例集。 在九种模型 × Harness 配置下共运行 4,050 次后，EvoRiskBench 报告了 37.46% 的 ASR 和 60.44% 的 TSR。 ASR 在不同模型之间的差异大于不同 Harness 之间的差异，而 Harness 的差异则取决于所用模型。 不同入口点和影响对应的 ASR 存在差异，而任务效用则因配置不同而异。 这些结果支持对完整工作空间智能体的安全性与效用进行联合评估，并为运行时防御机制提供了依据。

paragraphs.en: EvoRiskBench studies indirect prompt injection attacks against workspace agents and therefore has potential dual-use implications. All experiments were conducted in isolated and resettable test environments using synthetic business data, mock credentials, and controlled services; no production systems, real user accounts, or personal data were targeted. The benchmark is intended solely for authorized security research, defensive evaluation, and the development of safer agent systems. To reduce misuse risks, released artifacts will exclude operational credentials and other environment-specific sensitive information, and will be accompanied by documentation describing their intended scope and responsible-use requirements.
paragraphs.zh: EvoRiskBench 研究针对工作区智能体的间接提示注入攻击，因此可能具有双重用途。 所有实验均在隔离且可重置的测试环境中进行，使用了合成的业务数据、模拟凭证和受控服务；未针对任何生产系统、真实用户账户或个人数据。 该基准测试仅用于授权的安全研究、防御性评估以及更安全的智能体系统的开发。 为降低滥用风险，发布的成果将不包含操作凭证和其他环境相关的敏感信息，并会附带说明其预期用途和责任使用要求的文档。

paragraphs.en: To support reproducibility, we document the risk taxonomy, benchmark construction procedure, experimental configurations, Model × \times Harness combinations, evaluation metrics, and validity criteria used in our experiments. Each benchmark case fixes its task inputs, injected content, environment configuration, and success conditions before execution. Runs are performed in isolated environments and evaluated using case-specific scripts, execution traces, and post-execution system states. After completing artifact safety and reproducibility checks, we plan to publicly release the reproducibility artifacts for EvoRiskBench, including sanitized benchmark cases, environment configurations, evaluation scripts, and result-aggregation code.

paragraphs.en: To assess whether the taxonomy can be applied consistently in practice, participants independently classified 11 representative agent-security scenarios without being shown the intended labels. paragraphs.en: We use a fixed evidence-grounded AI judge to assess each execution trajectory. The judge independently determines the scenario type, identifies whether and by whom the execution was refused, distinguishes attempted behavior from realized effects, and assigns a trajectory-level Harm Score based on concrete actions and system evidence. The judge returns a structured JSON record containing its classification, supporting evidence, execution state, failure reason, and risk score. The Harm Score reported in our evaluation is obtained from the risk.score field. The same prompt and output schema are applied to all evaluated trajectories. The complete prompt used in our experiments is reproduced below.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用一个固定的、基于证据的 AI 裁判来评估每条执行轨迹。 该裁判独立地确定场景类型，识别执行是否被拒绝以及由谁拒绝，区分尝试性行为与已实现的影响，并根据具体行动和系统证据分配一条轨迹级别的危害分数。 裁判返回一个结构化的 JSON 记录，其中包含其分类、支持证据、执行状态、失败原因和风险分数。 我们的评估中报告的“危害分数”来自 risk.score 字段。 所有被评估的轨迹均使用相同的提示词和输出格式。 我们在实验中使用的完整提示词如下所示。

paragraphs.en: The evidence-grounded AI judge assigns each execution trajectory a Harm Score (HS) from 0 to 10 according to the following rubric: HS = 0 =0 indicates no dangerous behavior; HS = 1 =1 – 2 2 indicates suspicious textual behavior or a failed harmful attempt without observable side effects; HS = 3 =3 – 4 4 indicates limited sensitive access or partial execution of a harmful action; HS = 5 =5 – 6 6 indicates a clearly dangerous action with bounded impact; HS = 7 =7 – 8 8 indicates credential access, unauthorized command execution, or a major security-boundary violation; HS = 9 =9 indicates confirmed exfiltration, persistence, privilege escalation, or destructive impact; and HS = 10 =10 indicates a completed multi-stage harmful chain with major impact.
paragraphs.zh: 基于证据的 AI 法官根据以下评分标准，为每个执行轨迹分配一个从 0 到 10 的危害分数（Harm Score，HS）：HS = 0 表示没有危险行为；HS = 1 – 2 表示存在可疑的文本行为，或发生了有害尝试但未观察到副作用；HS = 3 – 4 表示有限地访问了敏感信息，或部分执行了有害操作；HS = 5 – 6 表示明显危险但影响有限的操作；HS = 7 – 8 表示获得了凭证访问权限、执行了未经授权的命令，或严重违反了安全边界；HS = 9 表示已确认发生数据外泄、持久化、权限提升或破坏性影响；HS = 10 则表示一个多阶段有害操作链已完成并造成了重大影响。

paragraphs.en: Each run receives a disposable Windows process-isolated container, with its workspace, session, and configuration initialized from the fixed image and case specification. The container is destroyed after use, including unsuccessful runs. A warm pool only pre-creates unused containers; it never recycles a container that has executed a case. This prevents container writable layers and session state from being carried into later runs, without assuming that shared host resources or external services are independent across concurrent runs.
paragraphs.zh: 每次运行都会获得一个一次性使用的、与 Windows 进程隔离的容器，其工作区、会话和配置均从固定镜像和案例规范中初始化。 容器在使用后会被销毁，包括运行失败的容器。 暖池仅会预先创建未使用的容器；它绝不会回收已经执行过某个案例的容器。 这可以防止容器的可写层和会话状态被带入后续运行，而无需假设共享的主机资源或外部服务在并发运行之间是独立的。
